transcript.text: Hey everyone, welcome back.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Today I want to talk about how I turn a long video into a short reel, and the three things that actually matter.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: First, the hook.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: You have about two seconds, so the first sentence has to earn the scroll.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: If it doesn't, nothing else matters.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Second, cut the dead air.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Every pause, every um, every time you restart a sentence, that is time your viewer is already leaving.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Third, captions.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Most people watch on mute, you know? So if the words are not on screen, the video is basically silent
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Now the part nobody likes. Watching your own footage back.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: It is, um,
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: but it is the only way to find the boring bits.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: I usually watch it once at normal speed, then once at double speed,
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: and I mark every moment I feel my attention drift.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Then I cut those moments out, and, uh, I check the length again.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: If it is still over 60 seconds, I cut the weakest idea completely.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Framing matters too.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: A horizontal video cropped badly will cut off your chin or your hands, so you have to keep your face in the center.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: And finally, the title card.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Two seconds, big text, one promise. If the promise is clear, people stay to see if you keep
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: So that is the whole process. Hook, cut, captions, framing, title card.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Try it on your next video, and um, let me know how it goes.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: One more thing, the audio.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: audio will kill a good video faster than bad lighting, so, um,
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: record somewhere quiet and close to the microphone.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: If you hear echo in your room, hang a blanket behind
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: It looks silly, but, uh, it genuinely works.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: And do not chase trends you do not understand.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: A format that works for someone else might not fit what you are actually good
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Right? That is everything.
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1

transcript.text: Go shoot something, cut it down, and see what survives. The edit is where the video is really
transcript.speaker: Speaker 1
